patterns.key_values: chromeless — no toolbar bar; controls dissolved into 4 floating Liquid Glass islands (traffic-light capsule, sidebar-toggle square, bottom segmented switcher, import FAB); monochrome SF Symbols; single trailing action
freeform spatial canvas (Infinity mode), not snapped; opaque items ~6-8pt radius, soft shadow, generous uneven whitespace; user imagery carries all colour

signature_moves: Chromeless content-first shell — all UI dissolved into 4 floating Liquid Glass islands over edge-to-edge imagery; sidebar collapsed; the collection IS the interface. Honours the glass Golden Rule cleanly (glass only on islands, content opaque).
Zero-accent UI — chrome contributes ~no colour; selection/emphasis neutral white-on-graphite not system blue; every thumbnail becomes figure against a silent frame (Von Restorff by subtraction).
Floating dark-glass view-mode switcher (Grid/Canvas/Infinity) — spatial browsing modes as core identity; Infinity freeform canvas is the hero mode.
Personable centered title ('HELLO, ATLAS' / '869 ITEMS') — Photos-schema window title made warm; the only chrome typography.
defects: Contrast Dilution (mild) — '869 ITEMS' subtitle gray on white borderline <4.5:1; sidebar-toggle glyph likely <3:1. The risk a near-white zero-accent shell courts; fix by pushing subtitle to #000@50% and darkening the glyph.

aesthetic.direction: Neo-grotesque product minimalism pushed to gallery-neutral — Restrained colour strategy at its limit, near-white ground, loose density, Liquid Glass depth, SF Pro tracked caps as the only type voice

psychology: Von Restorff / signal-detection — stripping UI colour makes every coloured thumbnail the figure; the gallery pops because the frame is silent
Jakob's Law — coloured traffic lights + centered title + count reads instantly as a native Mac gallery (Photos schema), zero learning cost
Hick's Law (well-applied) — view modes reduced to 3 and chrome to 4 controls; decision points minimal without thinning the content workspace
Progressive disclosure — sidebar collapsed and controls hidden as floating islands until needed, foregrounding content
Aesthetic-usability effect — airy near-white polish buys perceived usability/trust on first contact (with the contrast-floor caveat above)
